GitHub Copilot changed models. Your workflow still needs a test.

GitHub listed six model retirements for October 19. Supported alternatives keep you working; they don't prove your output still meets the brief.

This week: rerun one saved brief, compare against your accepted example, and review before expanding. The unit of progress is a working workflow, not a model name.

Draw from a range of premium looks (do NOT default to the same person-at-a-desk shot every time), for example: a confident Black creator/host presenting direct-to-camera; a close detail of premium creator gear (mic, stream deck, dark walnut desk, the standalone 8 motif on a hoodie or mug); an over-the-shoulder build session; an abstract Afrofuturistic tech or data-visualization environment with glowing electric-blue nodes and grids; or an atmospheric branded studio space. AI FLUENCY ADD-ON: grounded physical abstraction of model interchange and workflow evaluation, no person. GitHub Copilot retired models. Here's the workflow check worth keeping.

GitHub's notice listed six retirements for October 19, with suggested replacements including GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-5.6 Luna, Gemini 3.8 Flash, and Grok 4.6.

What changed: older choices are being removed across Copilot experiences.
What it does: supported alternatives let you continue the work; organization policies can affect access.
Why builders should care: a replacement model doesn't automatically preserve your output quality.

On Tech Thursday, Copilot CLI connected through MCP to create an image batch. The images arrived, but the look missed our standard. A successful tool call wasn't a successful creative result.

Try this week:
1. Identify the retired model in your saved workflow notes.
2. Check GitHub's suggested replacement and your organization's access.
3. Rerun one non-sensitive task with the same brief and an accepted example.
4. Compare the result, review the first output, and record what needs adjusting.

For code, check behavior and tests. For imagery, check subject, lighting, and framing. Same habit, different evidence.

The bigger signal: as AI moves into workflows, repeatable evaluation matters more than attachment to a model name.

Save this for your next AI stack change.
